payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow designs. Its independently audited, corrected cycle life is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge. The cell’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. At projected 500 MWh manufacturing scale, stack-level cost is $61/kWh. The chemistry has an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C, below which the thalliline dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
